name: Mobile equipment preventive maintenance
summary: Every 250 engine hours or so, each loader, truck, jumbo, bolter and drill in the underground fleet is taken out of production for a planned service: oils and filters are changed, the unit is greased and inspected, oil samples go to a laboratory and defects are fixed or put on the backlog. The planner turns hour-meter readings into work orders and kits the parts, the maintenance supervisor negotiates the release of the unit with the mine, and heavy-duty mechanics do the work in the underground bay or surface shop. The service is often delayed because production will not release the unit, a kit item is missing or the unit needs more repair than planned, and the paper work order card is typed into the CMMS days later.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer with one ramp-and-shaft underground mine, a 1,000 t/d class mill, about 300 employees on 14-on/14-off rotations living in camp, and a CMMS (ERP maintenance module) fed from paper work order cards.
baseline.notes: About 32 owner heavy units and 23 light vehicles in 2022 (er2022); contractor units are serviced by the contractor and are outside this process.

trigger: The CMMS forecast shows a unit within about a week of its next service hours and the work order is placed on the weekly schedule.
end_state: The unit is back in production, the work order is closed in the CMMS and the oil analysis has been reviewed, with any follow-up work request raised.

volume.seasonality: Even through the year; dips when production pauses during mill shutdowns are taken up by catch-up services.

evidence.note: 32 owner heavy units at 350-450 engine hours a month on a 250-hour interval give 45-58 heavy services, plus 23 light vehicles serviced every two to three months; hvi2026 gives a 250-hour service every two to three weeks at mining hours. Matches the organisation file.

er2022 lists 12 owner mine maintenance staff for the underground fleet in 2022; the organisation file has 22 heavy-duty mechanics. FTE on PM estimated from hands-on time with pairs on larger services.
Release negotiation and sign-off, about 25 minutes per PM.
Meter entry, packages, kit reservation, card entry and oil report review, about 80 minutes per PM.
Kit picking, about 25 minutes per PM.
One PM in ten needs an order.
Operators tram units to and from the shop; LHD operator stands in for all equipment operators.

systems.name: Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)
Mid-market ERP for finance, purchasing, inventory and fixed assets
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Shared drives and document library (procedures, permits, drawings)
Incident, inspection and training records system

steps.name: Key hour-meter readings into the CMMS
steps.description: The maintenance planner collects the hour-meter readings that operators write on their pre-shift inspection cards and shift sheets, and types the latest reading for each unit into the CMMS so that the PM forecast moves forward. Readings are entered in a batch two or three times a week because underground units have no live data link.

error.defect_description: A reading is mistyped or missing, so the service is forecast late or early.

evidence.note: ballantyne2019 notes underground equipment hours are recorded by shift; manual entry from paper cards in 2019-2022 is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Generate the PM work order
steps.description: The CMMS compares the forecast hours with the service interval (250, 500, 1,000 or 2,000 hours) and creates a preventive work order with the task list for that service level when the unit is within about a week of the due hours.

evidence.note: Tiered 250-hour services are standard; the lead time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare the work order package
steps.description: The planner prints the work order, adds the OEM checklist for the service level, attaches open backlog defects for the same unit so they are done during the stop, and writes the estimated hours. A unit that needs a large service is flagged for a longer release window.

error.defect_description: A backlog defect for the unit is missed and the unit is stopped again later.

evidence.note: Planner work content estimated from common CMMS practice at mid-size mines; the planner works office hours, so Friday work waits until Monday.

steps.name: Check and reserve the PM kit
steps.description: The planner looks up the filters, oils, grease and wear parts for the service in the ERP inventory, reserves them against the work order and sends a stores request to the warehouse. If a filter or kit item is short, a purchase requisition is raised.

error.defect_description: The reservation is booked to the wrong unit or a superseded part number.

evidence.note: hvi2026: a job is not ready until its parts are on the shelf; the 10% shortage rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Order the missing kit item
steps.description: The buyer turns the requisition into a purchase order to the dealer or OEM, asks for expedited freight to site and records the promised date on the work order so the planner can move the service if needed.

error.defect_description: The order goes to the wrong branch or without the rush flag.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for a remote northern Ontario site buying from dealers in Sudbury, Thunder Bay or Timmins.

steps.name: Wait for the supplier delivery
steps.description: The dealer ships the part by courier or the site's scheduled freight truck along the highway and mine road. Snowstorms and road closures in winter add days.

evidence.note: Two to seven days by road freight to a site an hour from the nearest town; author's estimate.

steps.name: Pick and stage the PM kit
steps.description: The warehouse attendant picks the reserved filters, oils and parts, issues them to the work order in the ERP and places them in the labelled bin for the unit in the underground or surface shop.

error.defect_description: A filter is left out or the wrong viscosity oil is staged.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of picking and transport time to the shop.

steps.name: Agree the release window with the mine
steps.description: At the shift line-up the maintenance supervisor asks the underground shift supervisor to release the unit for the scheduled day and time. The mine refuses when the unit is needed to muck a blasted stope or keep a heading cycle going, and the service is pushed back.

next.condition: mine keeps the unit for production; retry next shift or day

evidence.note: ballantyne2019 describes opportunity maintenance and arbitration between operations and maintenance over service events; the 20% refusal rate is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Tram the unit to the shop
steps.description: The operator finishes the current cycle, parks the bucket or boom and trams the unit up or down the ramp to the underground service bay or to the surface shop for large services, then hands the keys to the mechanic.

evidence.note: Ramp access with grades up to 15% and a surface mobile shop from er2022; travel times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Lock out, chock and assess hazards
steps.description: The mechanic chocks the wheels, lowers or blocks the bucket, boom and dump box, applies a personal lock and tag to the isolation switch and verifies that the machine cannot start. A short written hazard assessment is completed before work starts.

error.defect_description: An energy source is missed, for example stored hydraulic pressure.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 107(2) (chocks during maintenance), s. 108(2) (blocking raised parts) and s. 185(7)-(8) (lock, tag and verify energy isolation)

evidence.note: Duties stated in the regulation; time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Change oils and filters and grease
steps.description: The mechanic drains and refills the oils and changes the filters required at this service level (engine, transmission, hydraulic, axles at the larger services), greases every point, checks belts and records fluid levels on the checklist. Larger services are done by a pair; times here are the lead mechanic's.

error.defect_description: A filter is not seated or a fill level is wrong.

evidence.note: Fleet make-up and two 12-hour shifts from er2022; the 250-hour service as a standard status from ballantyne2019. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Take oil samples
steps.description: While the oils are hot the mechanic draws samples from the engine, transmission, hydraulics and differentials, labels each bottle with unit, hours and compartment, and fills in the lab form for shipment with the site freight.

error.defect_description: A bottle is mislabelled or a compartment is skipped.

evidence.note: Oil analysis on each service is common practice for mine fleets; author's estimate.

steps.name: Inspect the unit against the checklist
steps.description: The mechanic works through the inspection checklist: brakes and accumulators, steering, articulation joint, tyres and rims, hoses, frame cracks, fire suppression system, lights, guards and the operator cab. Each defect is written on the card as fixed now, needs parts or can wait.

error.defect_description: A developing defect such as a hose chafe or frame crack is not noticed.

next.condition: minor defect fixed during the stop
defect needs parts not in the kit
a component reaches its change-out hours

evidence.note: Defect rates are the author's estimate for an ageing mid-size fleet.

steps.name: Repair defects found
steps.description: The mechanic repairs the defects that can be done during the stop: replaces a hose or light, adjusts brakes, re-torques bolts or swaps a worn cutting edge, using parts from shop stock or brought from the warehouse.

error.defect_description: The repair is incomplete and the defect returns as a breakdown.

evidence.note: Fleet make-up and two 12-hour shifts from er2022; the 250-hour service as a standard status from ballantyne2019. Times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Request parts and decide whether the unit can run
steps.description: The mechanic raises a stores request or work request for the missing part and asks the supervisor whether the defect is safe to defer. If the part is on site the repair goes ahead after it is fetched; otherwise the defect goes to the backlog and the unit runs if it is safe.

error.defect_description: A defect that should stop the unit is deferred.

next.condition: safe to defer; work request to backlog

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Change out a component for rebuild
steps.description: When an engine, transmission, torque converter or final drive reaches its planned life, the mechanic removes it, fits the exchange unit from stores and tags the old component with unit, hours and reason before it is sent to the rebuild process.

error.defect_description: The exchange unit has the wrong configuration or the core tag is missing.

evidence.note: Component change-out hours and frequency are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Test brakes and functions and remove locks
steps.description: The mechanic removes the locks, starts the unit, checks for leaks and warning lights, tests the service, emergency and parking brakes as the regulation requires and confirms the fire suppression system is armed.

error.defect_description: A brake test is passed on a marginal brake.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 105(b) and s. 119.1 (service, emergency and parking brakes able to stop and hold the vehicle and each testable) and s. 185(7) for removing locks

evidence.note: Brake duties stated in the regulation; time and failure rate are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Sign off and release the unit
steps.description: The maintenance supervisor reads the completed checklist and defect notes, signs the card and radios the underground shift supervisor that the unit is available again.

error.defect_description: The supervisor signs without reading the deferred defects.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

steps.name: Tram the unit back to the work area
steps.description: An operator collects the unit and trams it back to its heading or stope. If the area has just been blasted, the operator waits for the re-entry time and ventilation clearance before going in.

evidence.note: Ramp layout from er2022; times are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Write up the work order card
steps.description: At the end of the shift the mechanic completes the paper work order card: start and finish times, meter reading, parts used, defects found and repaired, and any new work requests, and drops it in the planner's tray.

error.defect_description: Times or parts are left blank or written illegibly.

evidence.note: Paper cards re-keyed by planners were common in 2019-2022 at mid-size mines; author's estimate.

steps.name: Close the work order in the CMMS
steps.description: The planner types the card into the CMMS: labour hours by person, parts against the issue record, the new meter reading, defect codes and any follow-up work requests, then closes the work order. Unclear cards are sent back to the mechanic at the next rotation.

error.defect_description: Hours or parts are posted to the wrong work order, distorting cost history.

evidence.note: Office-hours planner clearing a weekly pile of cards; author's estimate.

steps.name: Wait for oil analysis results
steps.description: The samples travel with the weekly freight to the dealer or commercial laboratory, which tests them for wear metals, contamination and viscosity and emails a report graded normal, caution or critical.

evidence.note: Turnaround of three to ten days from the site is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Review the oil analysis report
steps.description: The planner reads the report, files it against the unit and compares wear metals with the unit's history. A caution or critical result is passed to the supervisor for a follow-up inspection or resample.

error.defect_description: A caution result is filed without action.

evidence.note: Author's estimate of abnormal result rate.

steps.name: Raise a follow-up work request
steps.description: For an abnormal result the planner raises a work request for an inspection, resample or component check, sets its priority with the supervisor and adds it to the backlog for the next weekly schedule.

error.defect_description: The priority is set too low and the component fails first.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Unit not released by production
exceptions.description: The mine keeps the unit for a shift or more and the service runs over its due hours.

exceptions.name: Kit item short
exceptions.description: A filter or part is ordered and the service waits for road freight.

exceptions.name: Defect needs parts
exceptions.description: A defect found at inspection needs a part not in the kit; it is repaired after fetching or deferred to the backlog.

exceptions.name: Planned component change-out
exceptions.description: A major component at the end of its life is swapped and sent for rebuild during the service.

exceptions.name: Brake or function test fails
exceptions.description: The unit goes back to repair before release.

evidence.note: Both describe the 250-hour service as the standard minor service.

benchmarks.unit: hours the unit is out of production per service

evidence.note: Minor 250-hour services take about 4-6 hours of work and larger services a shift or more, plus tramming, defect repairs and waiting for sign-off; the simulation holds the unit about 13.5 hours on average.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from work order creation to oil report review

evidence.note: About a week from work order to service, two to three days for card entry and about a week for oil results; not measured.

pain_points.description: PM competes with production for machines; the mine often keeps a unit past its due hours.

evidence.note: Opportunity maintenance and arbitration between operations and maintenance are described in ballantyne2019.

pain_points.description: Hour readings and work order cards are on paper and typed in by planners days later, so forecasts and cost history lag.

evidence.note: Author's estimate for 2019-2022 underground sites without equipment telemetry.

pain_points.description: Missing kit items and parts for defects stretch a planned stop into days.

evidence.note: Parts readiness as the main condition for a ready job.

pain_points.description: Oil results arrive after the unit is back at work, so abnormal wear is acted on a week late.

evidence.note: Remote site with weekly freight; author's estimate.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (NI 43-101, effective date December 31, 2021)
sources.publisher: SRK Consulting (Canada) Inc. for Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd.
sources.supports: Owner underground fleet of 55 units (3 two-boom jumbos, 2 blockholers, 17 LHDs of 2 to 6 yd, 3 30-t trucks, 3 scissor lifts, 4 production drills, 23 light vehicles) plus 17 contractor units (Table 16-9); owner underground labour 111 including 12 mine maintenance and 8 mine electricians, plus 36 contractors (Table 16-10); underground mine scheduled 365 days a year on two 12-hour shifts; ramp access with 30-t trucks and a three-compartment shaft with a double-drum hoist, hoisting at most about 16 hours a day; ore trucked 16.6 km from the portal to the mill; mobile maintenance shop and an asset management and planning office (new in 2021) on site; mill planned at 93.3% availability but 86% in 2021 because of a planned August 2021 shutdown to replace the cone crusher and trash screen, inspect and reinstall the secondary ball mill gearbox with motor alignment and liner inspection, inspect the fine ore bin and repair the coarse ore bin; average throughput 779 t/d.

sources.title: R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 854: Mines and Mining Plants, under the Occupational Health and Safety Act (consolidated text)
sources.supports: s. 105 (vehicles in safe working condition with brakes that stop and hold under full load); s. 106(4) (operators test service and emergency brakes before using a main ramp); s. 107(2) (wheel chocks whenever a vehicle is maintained or repaired); s. 119.1 (service, emergency and parking brake systems each testable); s. 158 (written locking and tagging programme for electrical work); s. 185(7)-(9) (moving parts stopped, stored energy dissipated, energy isolating devices locked and tagged and verified by testing before work on a machine); s. 82 (hoisting suspended and protection provided when work is done in a shaft compartment); s. 228(2) (drum hoist rope tests at intervals of not more than six months); s. 229(4) (two test trips after rope attachments are reinstalled); s. 248 (daily, weekly, monthly, six-monthly and twelve-monthly examinations of hoisting plant by competent persons, recorded in the Hoisting Machinery Record Book). Read in its current consolidation; the cited duties were in force in 2019-2022.

sources.title: Challenging the Norms: Time Usage Model for Mobile Underground Mining Equipment (white paper)
sources.publisher: RAK Developments (Ray Ballantyne), hosted by AusIMM
sources.supports: Underground mines on 2 x 12-hour shifts record equipment status for all calendar hours; typical maintenance statuses include the 250-hour service and breakdowns by subsystem (engine, transmission, hydraulics); opportunity maintenance when a unit is not required by operations; service overrun beyond the scheduled end; sites record waiting for fitter and waiting for parts within maintenance stoppages; jumbos accumulate diesel hours while travelling and electric hours while drilling.

sources.title: Weekly Maintenance Scheduling for Mining Teams
sources.publisher: Heavy Vehicle Inspection & Maintenance (JRS Innovation Inc.)
sources.supports: Weekly cycle for mining maintenance: mid-week sweep of open work orders, defects and coming PMs; planning with hour estimates, parts and permits; a job is not ready until its parts are on the shelf; schedule loaded to 80-85% of crew hours and frozen after machine release windows are confirmed with operations; daily 15-minute check; end-of-week schedule compliance and break-in review; wrench time 25-35% without structured planning; healthy backlog 2-4 weeks; a 250-hour service on a truck running 5,000-7,000 hours a year comes due every two to three weeks. Published after the reference period; used as a description of common practice, not as a 2019-2022 measurement.

assumptions: touch_min records the lead mechanic's minutes. Larger services (500 hours and up) use a pair, so mechanic FTE (5.5) is set at about 1.4 times the lead's hands-on time multiplied by volume.
Resource use is recorded against the LHD pool, which is about half of the owner heavy fleet; trucks, jumbos, bolters and drills follow the same steps with similar times.
Contractor-owned equipment (17 units in 2022) is maintained by the contractor and is outside this process.
The cycle ends when the oil report has been reviewed, which is usually after the work order is closed; the unit itself is out of production for about 4-16 hours.
The organisation file lists only hd-mechanic and maint-supervisor; the planner, warehouse attendant, buyer and operators also take part and use the organisation file's role ids.
Loaded costs are the organisation file's (wage x 1.35 for hourly site roles, x 1.30 for staff).
